chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The hour on Friday during which a believer supplicates and is answered.' He said: 'Yes, when the Imam departs.' I said: 'Indeed, the Imam hastens and delays.' He said: 'When the sun declines.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific time on Friday when a believer's supplication is accepted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise window for accepted supplications on Friday, distinguishing the general 'hour of response' from the specific time of the congregational prayer. By anchoring the time to the sun's decline (Zawal) rather than the Imam's variable departure, the hadith provides a consistent, observable marker for believers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imam's guidance while maintaining practical certainty in worship.
